fixed.how: All exact, no result changes. power.py: one memo per power step now also keeps branch-circuit liveness (circuit_live(..., memo)) and each top-level supply answer (supply_ok depth 0), so the loads pass and the derived-field pass walk each chain once; loads reuses the path it walked for the circuit (_wall_circuit); mains_ok reads its record once; sync_energized calls set_if only when a field would change. lighting.py: one working-bulb list per fixture (_working, dim_for(..., work)), set_if only for changed fields. detectors.py: one backup voltage, mounting, power status and clock.now per detector per pass (power_status(..., voltage, is_mounted), expired(..., now), _condition). clocks.py: the local wall-clock time once per pass. common.py: every static-index predicate declares the fields it reads (INDEX_READS; declare_index for batteries, cables, charging, devices and physical's predicates) and furnish._prebuild_indexes builds all 27 electrical indexes at episode_start (order -100, before any hook writes) on plain records, instead of through a read view per entity in the setup hooks (18) and the first substep (7).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_every_index_predicate_reads_only_its_declared_fields (every predicate on every registry type's defaults and every record of 4 generated houses, gen 1 and 2, reads only its declared fields), test_the_indexes_are_built_at_episode_start_and_change_nothing (each index built at reset equals a scan; an hour ends in the same digest with and without the early build), test_a_power_pass_answers_as_an_unshared_walk_of_each_supply_chain (memoized supply / liveness / circuit answers equal unmemoized walks on 3 houses quiet, with a tripped breaker, a tripped GFCI, strips off and a grid outage), test_the_light_and_detector_passes_write_what_a_fresh_pass_derives. All fail on HEAD (new API). Exactness: the A/B in notes (1,215 spec trials, identical verdicts and digests).

fixed.item: G7, engine side (the 1 h wait metric): electrical.power ran in 458 of 480 substeps of a 1 h wait on houses 0-3 although most runs changed nothing (its idle probe answered False 456 times).
fixed.how: power._power_ignore: the power note ignores every temperature_c but a modelled cord's own (_modelled_cord: fixed_temperature, a provider, not a wall outlet; power reads no other temperature) and appliance displays: a clothes iron or griddle its domain keeps heating woke the power step every substep (190 of the probe misses). common.IdleNote: a run that writes keeps the note's snapshots (the probe still answers False until a run writes nothing, which refreshes them), so a system whose own writes come and go (cord temperatures, breaker heat) is no longer re-warmed from nothing after each write; an unchanged snapshot is kept without a deep copy, compared field by field (_matches, the same comparison as the dict equality it replaces).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_a_devices_own_temperature_does_not_wake_the_power_step_but_a_cords_does (a fixed-temperature device's temperature leaves the probe True, a modelled cord's makes it False; fails on HEAD) and test_a_run_that_writes_keeps_the_notes_snapshots (after a writing run and a quiet run, a neighbour's repeated write no longer wakes the lights step; fails on HEAD). Exactness: Tier1SweepAdoptionTests.test_idle_probes_are_exact, and probes on vs off on 12 generated houses (8 gen 1, 4 gen 2) x six waits (20.5 h): identical digests after every wait, and identical to the HEAD code's; power runs 12,438 -> 4,400 of 27,612 substeps.

fixed.item: Own finding while reworking the probes (exact idle probes): IdleNote cached its members' location ancestors per World version and entity count, so a member put on a new parent during a step (a lamp on a cart) left that parent out, and the parent's later move (the cart wheeled into a warmer room) went unseen: the lights probe answered True while a dimmed lamp's bulb heat should follow the new room.
fixed.how: common.IdleNote: members(w) keeps the per-count cache (an index changes within a step only on create/destroy); ancestors(w, members) is taken when quiet() first needs it after a run and kept until the next run (any later change of a member's chain is a write to the member or to an entity of that chain, which quiet() sees).
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_a_lamp_wheeled_on_a_cart_into_a_warmer_room_wakes_the_light_step (fails on HEAD: the probe answered True after the cart's move).

fixed.item: Electrical's side of the manipulation breakage row (velcro on a garden hose: three owners write `coiled`, electrical a word, plumbing_liquids a bool, manipulation the dict of its coil verb): the cord heat model read only the words tight/coiled/loose, so a cord in manipulation's coil loops or in over_under loops heated as if laid out (k 30 C instead of 55 / 95 C).
fixed.how: power.coil_word(rec) reads every owner's form: tight (tight, coiled, True, a strapped or hand-wrapped coil dict), loose (loose, over_under, an unstrapped coil dict), uncoiled (anything else, None, {}); _cord_k uses CORD_K[coil_word]. No reachable outcome changes today (plug_in rewrites an extension cord's word and manipulation's coil verb unplugs a plugged cord), but a staged or future coiled cord now heats as one. docs section 1.
fixed.test: PhaseOneFinishTests.test_an_extension_cord_coiled_by_any_owner_heats_as_a_coil (the twelve forms; under a heater for an hour a manipulation-coiled cord runs >10 C hotter than a laid-out one and a strapped coil scorches).

perf: All measured on one snapshot of the shared tree (scratch snapA = live tree with electrical at HEAD, snapB = the same with this round's electrical files), interleaved runs, minima, with the machine at 100 % CPU from other agents (25 python processes on 8 logical CPUs), so whole-tree absolute numbers are not comparable across times; only same-snapshot A/B deltas are reported. Electrical's share of the regression: ADOPT 0.550 -> HEAD 0.580 ms per substep (bench_systems 40 0 1 2 3 --domain electrical on archived trees the same day: power 0.234 -> 0.250, devices 0.022 -> 0.031). bench_systems loop (40 substeps x seeds 0-3, 5-6 interleaved process pairs, min per system): electrical 0.599 -> 0.474 ms per substep (-0.125, -21 %; now below ADOPT's 0.55); steady state (after the first substep) 0.533 -> 0.462; first substep 3.1 -> 0.7 ms (index builds moved to episode_start on plain records). Per system: power 0.260 -> 0.219, lights 0.127 -> 0.097, detectors 0.098 -> 0.064, devices 0.034 -> 0.014, clocks 0.035 -> 0.033, charging 0.043 -> 0.044 (noise), cells/smart_home unchanged. Whole-engine 1 h wait on houses 0-3 (G7's second metric; probes on; 3 interleaved rounds, best of 2): wall 1.74-1.75 -> 1.63-1.66 s, CPU (process_time) 1.125-1.141 -> 1.047-1.078 s; electrical system calls 213-255 -> 92-111 ms; electrical systems plus probes 263 -> 162 ms; power runs 458 -> 265 of 480 substeps (12 houses x 20.5 h: 12,438 -> 4,400 of 27,612). No result changes: the A/B of all 243 authored specs (own mode, seeds 0 1 2 41 97, 1,215 trials, same snapshot, electrical files and type data swapped, spec files equal) gives 0 verdict, failure-list or wrong-plan changes and identical idle, reference and wrong-plan final digests (1,205 pass on both sides; the 10 failing trials are T-8e57df5742271b-01 x5 and another domain's T-03d77bbfc281a4-01 x5, both from the verifier's NeverActed rule); 12 generated houses (gen 1 seeds 0-7, gen 2 seeds 0-3) reach identical digests after six waits (20.5 h) with probes on and off, and the same digests with the HEAD code.

requests.request: Recompile tasks/specs.jsonl (python -m house_sim --compile) for the edited spec T-8e57df5742271b-01 in tasks/authored/electrical__examples.json (wrong plan 1 replaced) and sign it as an edited spec in the P1 gate policy (tools/orchestration/gate_policy/); its verdict goes FAIL -> PASS on seeds 0, 1, 2, 41, 97 against the live verifier.

Optional, for the next perf round: World.static_index checks declared reads (reads=) only when it evaluates through a read view (strict mode), so an index built on plain records with an incomplete declaration goes stale silently outside strict mode. A cheap guard would be a strict-mode check in _matching's plain path too (evaluate once through a _ReadView and compare keys). Electrical guards its own declarations with tests/test_electrical.py test_every_index_predicate_reads_only_its_declared_fields; safety, climate, tools_vehicles, mechanisms and pets prebuild the same way.
